sections.title: One Clip Among Nine Thousand
sections.narration: It is past midnight, and the house is quiet except for the hum of two monitors. Hannah scrolls through the eleventh year, the ninth thousand video, faster than she can watch. Then she stops. One thumbnail, crooked, taken from the height of a kitchen counter. She presses play. Her hand rises to her mouth and stays there. In eleven years of video, there was only one where she could see her own face.

sections.title: Three, Two, One
sections.narration: Three weeks earlier, Leo turned twelve. The ring light hummed above the kitchen table, and Hannah lifted the phone on its little gimbal. "Three, two, one." Leo looked at the candles, not the lens. "Mom, can I have one birthday that isn't content?"

sections.title: The Kitchen Counter
sections.narration: The clip is four minutes long. The phone had been left on the counter, still recording, pointed at the kitchen table. Leo, six years old, is telling a long and serious dream about a whale that lived in the bathtub. At the edge of the frame, Hannah sits at her laptop, editing. She nods once. She never looks up. In eleven years of video, there was only one where she could see her own face. She watches it to the end, and then she watches it again.
